title: How do we make three kinds of angle on a grid?
description: A grid of dots has one point marked A. Lines are drawn from A to other grid points, and each opening is compared with a square corner and a straight line. This makes an acute angle, an obtuse angle and a reflex angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: the kind of angle depends on how wide the opening is, so compare it with a square corner and a straight line. Watch for students who think short arms make an acute angle.

video_script.why: The child makes an acute, an obtuse and a reflex angle by comparing each opening with a square corner and a straight line.
video_script.substitution: Choose the second grid point so that the opening is smaller than a right angle, between a right angle and a straight angle, or past the straight angle.
video_script.anchor: a grid of dots with the point A marked, as in the book
video_script.payoff_line: Each kind of angle is made by comparing its opening with a square corner and a straight line

final_answer.value: an acute, an obtuse and a reflex angle at A, each marked with a curve
final_answer.spoken: an acute, an obtuse and a reflex angle are made at the point eigh, each marked with a curve

hold_back: three angles marked with curves at A
never_show: a rule that short arms make an acute angle
maths_rules: right angle = 90°, straight angle = 180°, full turn = 360°
acute: more than 0° and less than 90°
obtuse: more than 90° and less than 180°
reflex: more than 180° and less than 360°
a reflex angle is the long way round: 360° − (the angle inside)
the question is open-ended: many grid points give a correct angle
video_script.design: One dot grid with the point A. The first arm stays; a teal opening shows acute, amber shows obtuse, rose shows reflex. A square corner and a straight edge are laid on each opening to check.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which points make an acute, an obtuse and a reflex angle?

<bookmark mark='straight'/>A straight line through the vertex is a straight angle, one hundred eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='use'/>We compare the opening of each angle with these two.
